review_problems_structured: Re-fetched 15 FR 6103 (FR 1950-09-12, govinfo original bytes); pars. 1-4 match APP.
MSA 1954 sec. 543(a) re-read: orders under repealed law continue "until modified by appropriate authority" - repeal alone did not end the order (producer correct).

Correction 1 (CR-6): the FACA backstop for the IDAB (par. 3) needs non-federal membership; the producer did not show it. Closed: MSA 1954 sec. 308 requires members "broadly representative of voluntary agencies and other groups" (68 Stat. 842). The statutory basis was repealed in 1961 (FAA sec. 642(a)(2)). If the board still existed on 1973-01-05, FACA ended it by 1975-01-05. APP EO search for the board name finds only EO 10159, 10610 and 10803, so no renewal.

Correction 2 (CR-7): par. 1 ends because later comprehensive re-delegations of the whole MSA/FAA subject were "modification by appropriate authority" (EO 10575 sec. 303(c); EO 10893 sec. 305; EO 10973 secs. 605-606). None of them names EO 10159, so this is CR-7 route 3 (comprehensive replacement), not a bare implied repeal.
Par. 4 council: federal members only; its object (the AID program) is gone.
what_remains_inferential: Ending of pars. 1, 2 and 4 is by implied supersession and loss of object, not express revocation; whether IDAB still existed in 1973 not traced (ended either way). Current delegation order (EO 12163) not retrieved.

review_problems: Same statuses, corrected reasoning. The producer says pre-1969 offenses are "long time-barred". The correct basis is as follows. Para. 1 ended a suspension, a completed repeal-type act (TC07). Para. 2 only restates that the MCM 1951 Table applies (its source is MCM 1951 as amended by EO 10565). Any present use of the old limits would flow from the later Manual's own savings proviso, which is a historical consequence and not this order's residual (TC04/TC08; cf. CR-4).

review_problems: Agree. Sec. 1 window closed 1965-10-24. Sec. 2 (returning servicemen) has no date of its own; its object is a "competitive position in the Postal Field Service" and a CSC-prescribed examination. Reviewer checked the Postal Reorganization Act myself: sec. 5(a) saves orders issued "by (i) any department or agency" whose functions were transferred and only "until modified, terminated, superseded ... or by operation of law" - a presidential order is not issued by a department or agency, and in any case sec. 2 cannot operate once USPS appointments are made under USPS procedures (39 U.S.C. 1001(b)), USPS employees are not title-5 employees (5 U.S.C. 2105(e)) and 39 U.S.C. 410(a) displaces federal employee law. Sec. 6(o) renames "postal field service" references to USPS but creates no competitive positions. USPS began operations 1971-07-01; producer's outer bound 1971-08-12 (one year after enactment, sec. 15(a)) is a safe outer limit.

review_problems: ['Consistency with V11_G_EVENT_X2_REV (EO 6868 held): X2 held EO 6868 because D.C. Reorg. Plan 1/1987 sec. III.B(1) transfers "functions related to the powers and duties" of NCHA "established pursuant to" the Alley Dwelling Act and EO 6868 "as amended" - powers that sit in EO 6868 para. 3. In the same review X2 accepted no/no for the designation, composition and name amenders (7784A, 8033, 9916, 10128, 9344) because "A membership designation is not among the functions carried to DPAH/DCHA". This order belongs to that class: its only clauses are (i) designation of the Commissioner as "the Authority", (ii) a deemed-continuation clause, (iii) the NCHA name, (iv) acting officers. It does not touch para. 3. So no/no is consistent with the 6868 hold; if the 6868 hold is later resolved toward continuation, that continuation is of para. 3, not of this order\'s text (TC09).', 'Correction of basis: CR-10 is a land-description ruling and is not the right ground; the ground is the functional distinction above plus the D.C. chain I read myself: Home Rule Act sec. 202(b) vested "All functions, powers, and duties of the President under the" Alley Dwelling Act in the Commissioner (so the presidential designation was overtaken by statute); sec. 714(a)-(b) would carry a "designation" forward to the Mayor only "except to the extent modified or made inapplicable by or under authority of law"; the NCHA functions were then moved to DHCD "pursuant to Reorganization Order No. 3 of 1975" (recited in the 1987 plan, which I re-fetched) and Plan 1/1987 sec. VI abolished NCHA (eff. 1987-12-15). The deemed-continuation clause bridged 1968/1970 designations only; the 1987 transfer works by its own terms on the functions NCHA then held (historical consequence, TC07/TC08). Latest cessation 1987-12-15.', 'Endpoint: EO 11571 restated every clause of EO 11401 and changed the acting sequence; it can serve as first cessation under CR-7 (comprehensive substitute), but I rest the result on the 1975/1987 endings, which close it regardless.']
review_problems_structured: Consistency with V11_G_EVENT_X2_REV (EO 6868 held): X2 held EO 6868 because D.C. Reorg. Plan 1/1987 sec. III.B(1) transfers "functions related to the powers and duties" of NCHA "established pursuant to" the Alley Dwelling Act and EO 6868 "as amended" - powers that sit in EO 6868 para. 3. In the same review X2 accepted no/no for the designation, composition and name amenders (7784A, 8033, 9916, 10128, 9344) because "A membership designation is not among the functions carried to DPAH/DCHA". This order belongs to that class: its only clauses are (i) designation of the Commissioner as "the Authority", (ii) a deemed-continuation clause, (iii) the NCHA name, (iv) acting officers. It does not touch para. 3. So no/no is consistent with the 6868 hold; if the 6868 hold is later resolved toward continuation, that continuation is of para. 3, not of this order's text (TC09).

Correction of basis: CR-10 is a land-description ruling and is not the right ground; the ground is the functional distinction above plus the D.C. chain I read myself: Home Rule Act sec. 202(b) vested "All functions, powers, and duties of the President under the" Alley Dwelling Act in the Commissioner (so the presidential designation was overtaken by statute); sec. 714(a)-(b) would carry a "designation" forward to the Mayor only "except to the extent modified or made inapplicable by or under authority of law"; the NCHA functions were then moved to DHCD "pursuant to Reorganization Order No. 3 of 1975" (recited in the 1987 plan, which I re-fetched) and Plan 1/1987 sec. VI abolished NCHA (eff. 1987-12-15). The deemed-continuation clause bridged 1968/1970 designations only; the 1987 transfer works by its own terms on the functions NCHA then held (historical consequence, TC07/TC08). Latest cessation 1987-12-15.

Endpoint: EO 11571 restated every clause of EO 11401 and changed the acting sequence; it can serve as first cessation under CR-7 (comprehensive substitute), but I rest the result on the 1975/1987 endings, which close it regardless.

Added: under the rewritten Convention, regulations need "the approval of the Parties" (art. III para. 3), and art. III para. 2 now covers investigations only, so the order's object ("actions ... taken pursuant to that paragraph" requiring presidential approval) no longer exists. The 1987 EO 12608 amendment of sec. 2 is a cleanup listing, not a revival (TC11).

It does not touch para. 3. So no/no is consistent with the 6868 hold; if the 6868 hold is later resolved toward continuation, that continuation is of para. 3, not of this order\'s text (TC09).', 'Correction of basis: CR-10 is a land-description ruling and is not the right ground; the ground is the functional distinction above plus the D.C. chain I read myself: Home Rule Act sec. 202(b) vested "All functions, powers, and duties of the President under the" Alley Dwelling Act in the Commissioner (so the presidential designation was overtaken by statute); sec. 714(a)-(b) would carry a "designation" forward to the Mayor only "except to the extent modified or made inapplicable by or under authority of law"; the NCHA functions were then moved to DHCD "pursuant to Reorganization Order No. 3 of 1975" (recited in the 1987 plan, which I re-fetched) and Plan 1/1987 sec. review_problems_structured: Consistency with V11_G_EVENT_X2_REV (EO 6868 held): X2 held EO 6868 because D.C. Reorg. Plan 1/1987 sec. III.B(1) transfers "functions related to the powers and duties" of NCHA "established pursuant to" the Alley Dwelling Act and EO 6868 "as amended" - powers that sit in EO 6868 para. 3. In the same review X2 accepted no/no for the designation, composition and name amenders (7784A, 8033, 9916, 10128, 9344) because "A membership designation is not among the functions carried to DPAH/DCHA". This order belongs to that class: its only clauses are (i) designation of the Commissioner as "the Authority", (ii) a deemed-continuation clause, (iii) the NCHA name, (iv) acting officers. It does not touch para. 3. So no/no is consistent with the 6868 hold; if the 6868 hold is later resolved toward continuation, that continuation is of para. 3, not of this order's text (TC09).

Correction of basis: CR-10 is a land-description ruling and is not the right ground; the ground is the functional distinction above plus the D.C. chain I read myself: Home Rule Act sec. 202(b) vested "All functions, powers, and duties of the President under the" Alley Dwelling Act in the Commissioner (so the presidential designation was overtaken by statute); sec. 714(a)-(b) would carry a "designation" forward to the Mayor only "except to the extent modified or made inapplicable by or under authority of law"; the NCHA functions were then moved to DHCD "pursuant to Reorganization Order No. 3 of 1975" (recited in the 1987 plan, which I re-fetched) and Plan 1/1987 sec. VI abolished NCHA (eff. 1987-12-15). The deemed-continuation clause bridged 1968/1970 designations only; the 1987 transfer works by its own terms on the functions NCHA then held (historical consequence, TC07/TC08). Latest cessation 1987-12-15.

review_problems: REVISED 2026-10-17 after coordinator follow-up (earlier verdict: reject_to_indeterminate, any-effect indeterminate). (1) Board's end solid: original sec. 9 sunset 1976-12-31, advanced to 1975-09-15 by EO 11878 sec. 1 (own FR 1975-09-16 excerpt); window closed 1975-03-31 (EO 11842). (2) Correction to the producer: the residual (AG applying EO 11803 criteria under EO 11878 sec. 3) did NOT end 1976-03-31. EO 11878 sec. 6 is a deadline (TC10), and Ford Library records show AG transmittals after it (third AG report forwarded 1976-05-13). (3) Gap now closed with my own re-fetch of NARA schedule NC1-429-82-1 (DOJ, Office of the Pardon Attorney, received 1982-04-28; same bytes as V11_C_TEMP_X4_REV's copy, sha256 d87e020e...): DOJ via OPA 'assumed the responsibility for concluding the unfinished business of the PCB' on 1975-09-16; 'The last group of PCB pardons was processed by President Ford on January 19,1977'; closeout sheets record each case's 'final disposition'; case files had been retired to the WNRC, and later letters from applicants were filed only as residual correspondence. So the transferred caseload was concluded by 1977-01-19, and the EO 11803 criteria residual ended then. (4) Durable status (TC06) checked: pardons and clemency discharges are still recognized (32 CFR 724.112; 38 CFR 3.12(i)), but they trace to Proclamation 4313 and presidential warrants, not EO 11803 (TC07/TC08). eCFR has no reference to EO 11803 or the Board. (5) TC16: R_C_DATED_PERIOD predicate fails for 11803 (its effect outlived the Board through EO 11878). The correct basis is the Board sunset plus documented completion of the transferred caseload (event-bounded), not a dated period.

review_problems: Answer to the challenge: the order has NO end on its own terms - it authorizes one export (the one proposed in NRC application XSNM-1060) with no time limit, so 'no' needs that export to have been made (or an independent legal bar). Correction: the producer's end date (1978-07-12, House rejection of disapproval) is when the authorization became usable, not when it ended; the end is the export itself, undated, by inference mid/late 1978. Shipment not documented (reviewer searches: WebSearch x5 incl. 'XSNM-1060' exact; FRUS full-text search for '7.6 tons', '7.6 tonnes', '7,638', 'XSNM-1060'; NRC ADAMS API refused by proxy). Supporting inference, which I accept as sufficient at medium confidence: Desai to Carter, 1979-02-10 (FRUS d126) complains only of clearance delays ('the clearance of the 7.6 tonnes ... took more than one year') and lists the 16.8-tonne and third applications as the outstanding ones; India's Jan 1979 aide-memoire (d120) calls it 'the previous application' and lists only XSNM-1222 and XSNM-1379 as pending; Carter's 1980 message deals only with the later applications. R_C_EVENT_BOUNDED predicate 'event documented or necessarily past' is not strictly met; rule should read 'documented or shown by consistent contemporaneous official sources' or 12055 should stand alone.

review_problems_structured: Para. (2) end date 1943-06-30 is not proved as the end of payments 'made under the provisions of' NIRA: EO 9357 (effective 1943-07-01) transferred PWA functions together with 'the unexpended balances of the appropriations, allocations, or other funds' to the Federal Works Administrator, so liquidation payments from NIRA funds could continue after 1943 (later GSA, 1949). Record the date only as a bound (TC13): new Title II program authority ended 1943-06-30; last NIRA-fund payment date unknown; status unaffected.

Para. (2) ending ground is sound but should add the account-closing rule: no-year appropriation accounts are closed and balances canceled once purposes are carried out and no disbursement is made for two consecutive fiscal years (31 U.S.C. 1555), so no NIRA appropriation can fund a payment today; 31 U.S.C. 3526(c)(2) has a fraud exception and (c)(4)(A) leaves recovery from payees open, but neither gives the order a present object: any charge against a 1930s-40s officer is barred (28 U.S.C. 2415) and is a historical consequence (TC04/CR-4).
Confidence 'high' overstates para. (2): that no NIRA-fund payment remains is inferred from statutory termination and account-closing law, not records; medium is more accurate. Status unaffected.

All four CR-1 elements are met. On element 2, revival would need a new act, and a Secretary's charter under 50a is a separately authorized act, not EO 6750-C. Confidence on the committee can be raised.", "Rule (1)'s certificate runs 'until and unless such certificate is revoked'. review_problems_structured: Gap closed (CR-1, lane test d): the producer left the committee lineage untraced (medium confidence). Official FR: the Federal Committee on Apprenticeship (FCA), the Secretary's apprenticeship committee, was renewed under FACA in 1996 with an employer/labor/public membership unlike EO 6750-C's (Office of Education, NRA, DOL) (61 FR 4491). Its charter 'expired on January 26, 1998' and a newly chartered FCRA 'succeeds' it (64 FR 3572, 1999). Since 1937, 29 U.S.C. 50a has given the Secretary independent power to 'appoint national advisory committees'. So even if the 1934 committee was the FCA's ancestor, any such body ended by charter expiry in 1998. Every later committee (FCRA, ACA) is a new act under 50a and FACA (TC08/TC11). All four CR-1 elements are met. On element 2, revival would need a new act, and a Secretary's charter under 50a is a separately authorized act, not EO 6750-C. Confidence on the committee can be raised.

Rule (1)'s certificate runs 'until and unless such certificate is revoked'. The footprint should record that this is a durable term with no own end, and test it under TC06. It fails TC06: the certificate's only consequence was an exception to wages/hours 'established in such code' (and agreements), which ended by 1936-04-01. A certificate under FLSA 14(a) must issue 'pursuant to regulations of the Secretary', and no current CFR recognizes NRA-era certificates (eCFR 0 hits). Status unaffected.

review_problems: Same statuses. Corrections: (1) The producer did not read the 1950 Grand Teton Act. I fetched it (64 Stat. 849, ch. 950; now 16 U.S.C. 673b). Sec. 2 makes the former Jackson Hole National Monument lands (T.42N R.116W secs. 24-26, 35; T.42N R.115W parts of secs. 8-10, 17-19, and others) part of the National Elk Refuge by statute. Those EO 7680 lands that Proc. 2578 had superseded now rest on the Act, not on the order (TC08). The YES footprint is the EO 7680 lands that were never inside the monument (e.g. T.41N R.115W secs. 4-7, 17-19; T.42N R.115W secs. 1, 11-14), plus lands acquired under its proviso; the 1986 BLM notice applied that proviso to T.42N R.115W lands. (2) 2024-2026 agency sources: the FWS refuge page (2026) says the refuge 'was established by various Acts of Congress, executive orders, and other documents'. The FWS Draft EIS (Aug. 2026) lists the 1912, 1913 and 1927 Acts and EOs 3596 and 3741 but NOT EO 7680. That is counterevidence for the bridge, but not dispositive: EO 3741, which it lists, was itself revoked by EO 7680, and no instrument revoking or replacing EO 7680 was found. The 1927 Act (16 U.S.C. 673a) covers only the Izaak Walton League gift tracts, which the EO 7680 public-domain tracts complement. (3) Federal Register API searches (all years: 'National Elk Refuge' + withdrawal; + 'Executive Order') found no revocation. Bridge: 16 U.S.C. 668dd(a)(6) and 43 U.S.C. 1714(j). Medium confidence stays.

review_problems_structured: Rule S11D-R7 predicate P4 ('each EO 8557 clause is covered or contradicted by the current FTR') is NOT met as stated: current 41 CFR part 303-70 (FTR Case 2025-05) is silent on EO 8557 sec. 12 (notify next of kin, render assistance, inform them of the regulations), sec. 13 (pay directly or reimburse) and sec. 16 (Government bill of lading); the producer's P4 list skipped these clauses.

Gap closed by reviewer evidence: GSA's own FTR chapter 303 (codified by 54 FR 20351, May 10, 1989, from former FTR/FPMR 101-7 chapter 3, part 3-1; 1997 CFR text read) restated every EO 8557 clause as GSA regulation under 5 U.S.C. 5742(b) and EO 11609 sec. 1(13): notification/assistance (303-1.2), method of payment incl. GBL (303-1.7), absence from duty (303-1.5), escort bar (303-1.6), veterans proviso (303-1.4), other-law bar (303-2.8), household goods by reference to 302-8, definitions (303-1.3), with a different cap ($250 vs EO's $150). That is a complete substitute issued by the delegate empowered (EO 10530 sec. 7; EO 11609 sec. 10(c)) to amend, modify or revoke prior presidential regulations. Later GSA changes (1999 actual-cost rule; 2025 rewrite that dropped the notification duty) modified GSA's own text and cannot revive EO 8557 text (TC11 analogy). Statute now also contradicts sec. 15 (5 U.S.C. 5742(b)(3) authorizes up to 2 escorts).
Corrected end: superseded no later than 1989 (54 FR 20351) and probably earlier under FPMR 101-7 chapter 3 (pre-1989 text and first BoB/GSA substitute not read; first-cessation date unknown).

review_problems: ["Correction to rule S11D3-R1 predicate P3 (TC10): the 'terminal date' is a cutoff on APPLICATIONS (a certificate 'shall be issued only if application therefor is filed ... prior to' the date), not a sunset of the issuing power; on its face a timely application could still be acted on after the date. review_problems_structured: Challenge (f): the producer did not read the 1956 transition rules. Pub. L. 84-854 sec. 403, "CONTINUATION OF PRIOR RIGHTS", says the 1956 amendments do not apply to employees "retired or otherwise separated prior to its effective date, and the rights of such persons and their survivors shall continue in the same manner and to the same extent as if this title had not been enacted." So for the closed class of High Commissioner staff separated before Oct. 1956, the 1930 Act still governs, as EO 9616 para. 12 interprets it, and so do the rights of their survivors.

Substantive no: the crediting rule can no longer be applied to anyone newly entering service, because the 1956 sec. 3 credits only civilian service of the U.S. Government and current 5 U.S.C. 8332 has no "overseas"/Philippine wording. Any-effect: under the codebook's exception, a residual term with no proved surviving subjects gives an INDETERMINATE any-effect, not NO. It is not shown whether any survivor annuitant whose rights rest on para. 12 credit is still alive or being paid. Paras. 1-11 and 13-14 ended by 1946 (I agree).

Closure therefore rests on three further grounds, now evidenced: (1) the certificates speak only to the WWII 'emergency period', which Proc. 2669 ended on 1945-09-29; (2) 26 U.S.C. 7851(a)(1)(A) keeps 1939-Code ch. 1 (incl. sec. 124) only for taxable years before 1954, 7851(b)(1) preserves rights/liabilities (saved acts, TC08) and 7851(d) keeps the old limitation periods, so any certificate can affect only 1940-1953 years; (3) no pending timely application or current reliance found (APP, NARA, eCFR searched by producer). 7851 does not keep the orders' issuing authority alive in any present operative sense: it preserves the 1939-Code regime for closed years, i.e. historical consequences (TC04/TC07).

review_problems: Same statuses; I added a second, independent ending ground. The order rests on 'Title I of the First War Powers Act, 1941'. I re-read Title I (55 Stat. 838): - sec. 401 limits it to the war plus six months; - on termination, every agency 'shall exercise the same functions ... as heretofore or as hereafter by law may be provided, any authorization of the President under this title to the contrary notwithstanding'. review_problems: Same statuses. Added a second, independent ending ground: EO 9709 transferred War/Navy functions to Commerce under Title I of the First War Powers Act, 1941 (cited in the order). I re-read Title I. It was limited to the war plus six months (sec. 401), and 'Upon the termination of this title' every agency 'shall exercise the same functions ... as heretofore or as hereafter by law may be provided, any authorization of the President under this title to the contrary notwithstanding'. So the Title I transfer could not outlast Title I. Whatever continued did so under the International Aviation Facilities Act 1948 (sec. 8(c) deems EO 9709 property transferred under the Act). EO 11048 sec. 304 (1962, Wake and Midway administration; re-read) is a non-interference clause. It neither continues nor revives EO 9709 (TC11). Paras. 2-4 (arrangements, accepting funds, exercise by Commerce) are tied to the transferred facilities and fall with para. 1. Exact Title I termination date not fixed here (war ended Apr. 28, 1952); the 1948 Act is the latest-cessation instrument.

review_problems_structured: RE-REVIEW of the producer's revised record (yes/yes, medium), 2026-10-16.

The producer fetched the FAM page independently. Its original bytes have sha256 da54e36d1913e7dca3ba0bec2e6a20a340f259f7486a291e1ac5bcb11c4908cb, identical to my own retrieval (cache/fam_2fam0320.html).
All of the producer's new evidence quotes (X2-E130..E142B) are exact substrings of their files, and the sha256 values match (code/check_evidence.py, 126 records).

I agree with every predicate. 2 FAM 322 c (CT:GEN-617, 2025-04-16) says the rules "are based on Executive Order 9998". 2 FAM 325.1 a applies sec. 13 "In accordance with Executive Order 9998". 2 FAM 324.1-324.7 restate secs. 1, 2 and 4-9. FSA 1980 sec. 2401(a) continues the order. 22 U.S.C. 3927 makes chiefs of mission act under the President's direction. The presidential-power basis is valid because R.S. 1752 was already repealed in 1946.

Correction to my own earlier note: sec. 14 IS in the current FAM. 2 FAM 325.2 (CT:GEN-298) restates it (consular vs. PHS medical officers). It does so without naming the order, so only 322 c and 325.1 a apply the order by name.
Sec. 3 proviso (FAA 1948, repealed 1954) and sec. 15 (supersession) are spent. Sec. 13's "commodores" is adapted to "rear admirals" in the FAM. This is implementation of the order, not replacement.

Change check: NARA table (to 1989), APP searches, and federalregister.gov full text (1994 onward, 0 hits) found no revocation. The 1989-1994 gap was covered only by APP, which lists every executive order, so the gap is small. No Wayback pre-cutoff capture exists; the CT dates predate the cutoff.

Row 3 of its table is "June 4, 1856 | | Revoked by Proc. 2318"; rows 1, 9 and 10 match the packet's rows 1, 9 and 10, which confirms the row indexing.

Proc. 2318 (4 FR 75; APP) reaches the order WHOLE: "The Executive Order of June 4, 1856, withdrawing public land for lighthouse purposes, is hereby revoked." The same sentence group limits the EO 4430/6964 revocations "in so far as they affect" the forest lands, which shows the 1856 revocation was deliberately unqualified.
